Source: the identification of the varifold's tangent planes with those of the C^1 graph, used implicitly in Steps 2-4 of the parent-supplied proof ('on the graph region mu = theta H^n on the C^1 graph'); it is Simon Ch. 3, 1.4-1.9 (approximate tangent spaces) specialized to a C^1 graph: a C^1 graph has its classical tangent plane as approximate tangent plane, and a locally integrable multiplicity does not change this at its Lebesgue points. No mean curvature or multiplicity hypothesis is needed. Notation. mu := V.weight, M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, Sigma := V.support = U cap spt mu, H^n := muHE[n], omega_n := unitBallVolume n. Bo_r = open ball, B_r = closed ball. T(y) := Q(y - xi), A(z) := xi + Q^{-1} z = T^{-1}(z); G(x) := graphPoint x (u x) = (x, u(x)); Gamma := G(Bo^n_R(0)); pi : R^(n+l) -> R^n the projection onto the first n coordinates, so pi(G(x)) = x. For x in Bo^n_R(0), DG(x) v = (v, Du(x) v) is injective, tau_x := range DG(x) is an n-dimensional subspace, and for y with T(y) = G(x) put P_y := Q^{-1}(tau_x) = Submodule.map Q.symm (LinearMap.range (fderiv G x)), an n-dimensional subspace. The graph hypothesis T(Sigma) cap Bo_R(0) = Gamma cap Bo_R(0) means Sigma cap Bo_R(xi) = A(Gamma cap Bo_R(0)). J(P) := sqrt(det(I_n + (

)_{a,b})) = normDet of v -> (v, P v). Facts used. (Iso) H^n(T(S)) = H^n(S) and, for the dilation eta(w) = lam^{-1}(w - y), H^n(eta(S)) = lam^{-n} H^n(S) (Mathlib IsometryEquiv.hausdorffMeasure_image, hausdorffMeasure_homothety_image), hence integral over eta(S) of g dH^n = lam^{-n} integral over S of g(eta w) dH^n(w). (Lip) H^n(G(S)) <= Lip(G on S)^n L^n(S). (Area) area formula for G injective and Lipschitz on a set (simongmt Chapter02.injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn and its weighted forms; Bochner-integral versions follow by splitting into positive and negative parts): integral over G(S) of k dH^n = integral over S of k(G x) J(Du(x)) dx; linear version: integral over L(R^n) of k dH^n = integral of k(L v) normDet(L) dv. (LebPt) Lebesgue differentiation for a finite Borel measure nu on R^(n+l) (Besicovitch; Mathlib VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub for Besicovitch.vitaliFamily nu): for f in L^1(nu), for nu-a.e. y, (1/nu(B_r(y))) integral over B_r(y) of |f - f(y)| dnu -> 0 as r -> 0+. (F2) mu(R^(n+l) minus spt mu) = 0 (Mathlib Measure.measure_compl_support); mu = theta H^n on M with theta > 0 on M. (Uniq) simongmt Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique: weighted approximate tangent planes are unique where theta is nonzero. 1. Reduction. It suffices to prove, for each s' in (0, s), that the claim holds for mu-a.e. y in Bo_{s'}(xi): taking s' = s - 1/k (k large) and a countable union of null sets then gives the claim on Bo_s(xi). Fix s' in (0, s). 2. A finite graph piece. Gamma' := Sigma cap Bo_{s'}(xi) = A(G(D')) with D' := {x in Bo^n_R(0) : |G(x)| < s'}, an open set contained in Bo^n_{s'}(0) because |G(x)| >= |x|. The closed ball B^n_{s'}(0) lies in Bo^n_R(0) (s' < s <= R), is compact and convex, and Du is bounded on it, so G is L_G-Lipschitz on it for some L_G >= 1; by (Lip) and (Iso), H^n(Gamma') <= L_G^n L^n(B^n_{s'}(0)) < infinity. Gamma' is relatively closed in Bo_{s'}(xi), hence Borel. Let nu := H^n restricted to Gamma', a finite Borel measure. 3. mu has density f := theta 1_M with respect to nu on Bo_{s'}(xi). Bo_{s'}(xi) is contained in B_s(xi), contained in U, so Bo_{s'}(xi) minus Sigma = Bo_{s'}(xi) minus spt mu is mu-null by (F2). For Borel S contained in Bo_{s'}(xi): mu(S) = mu(S cap Sigma) = integral over S cap Gamma' cap M of theta dH^n = integral over S of f dnu. Moreover mu(Bo_{s'}(xi)) <= mu(B_s(xi)) < infinity, because B_s(xi) is a compact subset of U and theta is H^n-integrable on M cap B_s(xi); hence f is in L^1(nu). 4. Upper bound for nu on small balls. Let y in Gamma' and T(y) = G(x). If |G(x') - G(x)| <= r then |x' - x| <= r, so Gamma' cap B_r(y) is contained in A(G(D' cap B^n_r(x))) and nu(B_r(y)) <= L_G^n omega_n r^n by (Lip) and (Iso). 5. Good points. By (LebPt) and step 4, for nu-a.e. y in Gamma': r^{-n} integral over B_r(y) of |f - f(y)| dnu = (nu(B_r(y))/r^n) * (average of |f - f(y)| over B_r(y)) <= L_G^n omega_n * (that average) -> 0 (if nu(B_r(y)) = 0 the integral is 0). Let E be the set of y in Gamma' cap M with this property. The complement of E in Bo_{s'}(xi) is mu-null: mu(Bo_{s'}(xi) minus Gamma') = 0 (step 3), mu(complement of M) = 0, and the (LebPt) exceptional set is nu-null, hence mu-null since mu restricted to Bo_{s'}(xi) equals f nu (pass to measurable null supersets where needed). 6. Blow-up of the weighted carrier at y in E. Write T(y) = G(x) with x in Bo^n_R(0); then x = pi(T y) and x lies in D'. Put P := P_y. Let phi be continuous with compact support in B_{rphi}(0), and let 0 < lam < lam0 where B_{lam0 rphi}(y) is contained in Bo_{s'}(xi). By (Iso) for the dilation and step 3: I(lam) := integral over blowUpMap y lam '' M of phi(z) theta(y + lam z) dH^n(z) = lam^{-n} integral over M of phi((w - y)/lam) theta(w) dH^n(w) = lam^{-n} integral of phi((w - y)/lam) dmu(w) = lam^{-n} integral of phi((w - y)/lam) f(w) dnu(w) = f(y) lam^{-n} integral of phi((w - y)/lam) dnu(w) + Err(lam), with |Err(lam)| <= sup|phi| * lam^{-n} integral over B_{lam rphi}(y) of |f - f(y)| dnu = sup|phi| rphi^n (lam rphi)^{-n} integral over B_{lam rphi}(y) of |f - f(y)| dnu -> 0 by step 5. 7. Blow-up of the graph. By (Iso) with T and then (Area) with the substitution x' = x + lam v (on the compact set where G is Lipschitz): lam^{-n} integral of phi((w - y)/lam) dnu(w) = lam^{-n} integral over G(D') of phi(Q^{-1}(z - G(x))/lam) dH^n(z) = integral over {v : x + lam v in D'} of phi(Q^{-1}(G(x + lam v) - G(x))/lam) J(Du(x + lam v)) dv. Since |G(x + lam v) - G(x)| >= lam |v|, the integrand vanishes for |v| > rphi; it is bounded by sup|phi| times the bound of J(Du) on B^n_{s'}(0); and for each v it converges, as lam -> 0+, to phi(Q^{-1} DG(x) v) J(Du(x)) (D' is open and contains x, G is differentiable at x, phi and Du are continuous). By dominated convergence the limit is integral over R^n of phi(Q^{-1} DG(x) v) J(Du(x)) dv = integral over tau_x of phi(Q^{-1} z) dH^n(z) (linear area formula, normDet DG(x) = J(Du(x))) = integral over P of phi dH^n ((Iso) for Q^{-1}). 8. Conclusion at y in E. By steps 6-7, I(lam) -> f(y) integral over P of phi dH^n = theta(y) integral over P of phi dH^n (y is in M) for every compactly supported continuous phi, and finrank P = n. Hence HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta y P holds. Since theta(y) > 0 (y in M), (Uniq) shows that the plane chosen in the definition of V.tangentProj y equals P, so V.tangentProj y = P.starProjection. If x' in Bo^n_R(0) is any point with Q(y - xi) = graphPoint x' (u x'), then x' = pi(T y) = x, so the asserted identity holds for every such x'. By step 5 this holds for mu-a.e. y in Bo_{s'}(xi), and by step 1 for mu-a.e. y in ball xi s. This is the second conjunct. 9. Measurability (first conjunct). Let O' := {y in Bo_s(xi) : pi(T y) in Bo^n_R(0)}, an open set. For y in O' put x(y) := pi(T y) and p(y) := orthogonal projection onto Q^{-1}(range DG(x(y))); put p(y) := 0 for y outside O'. Since x -> DG(x) is continuous on Bo^n_R(0) and DG(x) is injective, the orthogonal projection onto its range, DG(x) (DG(x)^* DG(x))^{-1} DG(x)^*, depends continuously on x; conjugating by Q is continuous. Hence p is continuous on the open set O' and 0 off O', so p is Borel measurable, and it is strongly measurable because the space of continuous linear maps of R^(n+l) is finite-dimensional. For mu-a.e. y in Bo_s(xi) we have y in Sigma (Bo_s(xi) is contained in U and mu(Bo_s(xi) minus spt mu) = 0 by (F2)), hence T(y) = G(x) with x = pi(T y) in Bo^n_R(0) by the graph hypothesis, so y is in O'; and V.tangentProj y = p(y) for mu-a.e. such y by steps 1 and 8. Thus V.tangentProj = p almost everywhere for V.weight.restrict (ball xi s), and AEStronglyMeasurable (fun y => V.tangentProj y) (V.weight.restrict (ball xi s)) follows (AEStronglyMeasurable.congr).
